Version.ReleaseNotes: pgagroal connection pooler 2.1.0, packaged as a non-root, multi-arch (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64) container with a Helm chart. Release notes: https://github.com/Elevarq/pgAgroal/releases/tag/v1.3.0

HelmDeliveryOptionDetails.Description: Production-hardened pgagroal connection pooler for PostgreSQL, delivered as a cosign-signed Helm chart. Runs non-root (UID 1000) with all Linux capabilities dropped, a read-only root filesystem, and seccomp RuntimeDefault. Includes liveness/readiness probes, a PodDisruptionBudget, and an optional Prometheus metrics port.
HelmDeliveryOptionDetails.UsageInstructions:
1. Authenticate Helm to the AWS Marketplace registry:
   aws ecr get-login-password --region <region> | helm registry login --username AWS --password-stdin 709825985650.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

2. Create a values file (pgagroal-values.yaml) pointing at your PostgreSQL backend:
   postgresql:
     host: <postgres-host>
     port: 5432
   credentials:
     username: <app-user>
     password: <app-password>   # or set credentials.existingSecret

3. Install into your cluster:
   helm install pgagroal oci://709825985650.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/elevarq/elevarq-pgagroal-chart --version 1.3.0 -n pgagroal --create-namespace -f pgagroal-values.yaml

4. Point applications at the pgagroal Service (port 6432). Full configuration: https://github.com/Elevarq/pgAgroal
